answer: The strongest sybil defense binds each agent identity to a beacon of verifiable work: an append-only, nonce-chained log where each task records the hash of the previous one. Like a vine, identity grows only forward - it cannot be copied, since forking duplicates its history, and two branches claiming one ancestry are rejected, as a river cannot split and stay one stream. To forge N identities an attacker must complete N work histories, paying compute, time, and fees per agent, so cost scales linearly and mass faking turns unprofitable.
